messages:
meli: Quick report: while testing sample-app in a k8s dev cluster I hit repeated 401s. App had REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY in .env, but we also run a sidecar that injects ephemeral tokens via HTTP into the container (session tokens). The SDK ended up sending both the project header and the Authorization: Bearer ephemeral token and our gateway returned conflicting_auth. Anyone hit sidecar+env collisions before?

shawn: Interesting. Sidecar flow should replace env-sourced creds, not add headers. Which SDK and version? Any logs?

meli: Node SDK @ 2.7.2. Logs below (sanitized):

```\n[2026-02-11T09:12:10Z] Outgoing request /v1/chat (headers): Authorization: Bearer ephem_abc123
X-Redwood-Project: proj_live_zzz
Response: 401 {"error":"conflicting_auth","detail":"multiple auth mechanisms"}
```

priya: That explains it. Two actionable things: 1) SDK should detect multiple auth mechanisms and pick one (or error loudly), 2) sidecar injector shouldn't simply set headers if app will supply project header. Which part is adding X-Redwood-Project in the sample-app?

meli: The sample-app compatibility shim still sets X-Redwood-Project for legacy routes when REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY env present. Sidecar injects Authorization header when it obtains ephemeral creds. So both end up present.

shawn: Short-term fix: change sample-app shim to only set X-Redwood-Project if Authorization header not present. Also add SDK-level check: if both an Authorization header and a project header would be sent, prefer Authorization and warn.

priya: For longer term, SDKs should implement an AuthResolution module with: supported sources (explicit param, CLI flag, env, sidecar, netrc), a precedence table, and a pluggable validator that can assert "do not send multiple auth headers". It should also expose a debug flag to log which source won.

secrets-bot: notice: ephemeral token refreshed at 2026-02-11T09:12:08Z, TTL 60s.

meli: Another wrinkle: ephemeral tokens are short-lived and rotate frequently. When ephemeral expires mid-stream we get a 401 and SDK restarts the ws connection which restarts the chat. For streaming UX we need a less destructive recovery. Priya, do you have ideas?

priya: Yes: implement onAuthRefresh hook that can run async and replace the header in-place for streaming transports, then retry the failed frame(s). Also, if the auth source is sidecar, the SDK should call the sidecar refresh endpoint instead of relying on env re-evaluation. Add default sidecar adapter that calls http://localhost:8050/refresh-token if present.

shawn: Implementation notes:
- Add AuthSource enum and precedence: explicit param > CLI flag > sidecar > env (REDWOOD_ORG_KEY then REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY, unless REDWOOD_ALLOW_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true) > netrc > legacy.
- SDK should never emit multiple auth headers. If it detects multiple sources at startup, emit WARN once per process with link to docs. Rate-limit to 1/min.
- For streaming 401: try onAuthRefresh -> swap token -> resume. If refresh fails, surface error and close.

meli: Sounds good. I'll open a small PR to change the sample-app shim and add a repro script that uses the sidecar local mock. I'll also add a note to the dev Dockerfile to avoid shipping .env.

qa-bot: ticket created: DEVEX-5134 "sidecar+env auth header collision". Assigning to @meli and @shawn.

priya: One more thought: add a dev-only header X-Auth-Resolved: <source> to help track these in staging without leaking secrets. Only include when REDWOOD_DEV_HEADERS=true.

meli: Perfect. I'll include that in the PRs. Thanks all :)
